standard.title: Materials affect movement
standard.description: explore how technologies including materials affect movement in products
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can explore how products are designed by people (AC9TDEFK01). They have made simple solutions using materials (AC9TDEFP01). They have not yet systematically connected material properties to movement outcomes, or explored how changing materials or forces changes how a product moves.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how material properties and forces affect movement in products, and explain how changing materials can change how a product moves.

nodes.label: Material properties and movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how a material's properties affect how a product moves
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one material property (e.g. smooth, rough, flexible, rigid) and explain how it affects movement in a product or on a surface
nodes.typical_width: Explore multiple material properties (smooth/rough, light/heavy, flexible/rigid) and explain how each affects movement; select materials to show how properties are appropriate for particular movement outcomes (sliding, floating, flying)
wider: Investigate First Nations Australians' instructive toys and how they are designed and made to produce movement — for example propeller toys made from pandanus across northern Australia; identify which materials are used and how their properties create the movement
Test a wheeled toy on different surfaces (timber, carpet, rubber, plastic) — measure or observe differences in movement and speed; explain how surface material properties affect movement

response_modes.reason: Students at Y1-2 may connect a specific material to a specific toy without generalising to the property relationship — 'the smooth floor makes it go fast' without understanding that smoothness (low friction) is the relevant property. Multiple material-movement contexts where the same property appears in different products builds the generalised property concept.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The First Nations propeller toys direction is rich — it connects material-movement knowledge to purposeful, culturally situated design, and the pandanus material properties are genuinely interesting to investigate alongside modern materials.
success_criteria: Names at least one material property
Explains how that property affects how a product moves
nodes.hinge_reason: Without the material-property concept, Node 2's integration of material properties with forces has no anchor — students who cannot generalise from specific examples to a property cannot reason about how property and force interact.

nodes.label: Combining materials and forces to create movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore how combining materials with forces creates movement in a product
nodes.minimum_width: Using one product (e.g. a toy boat, kite or puppet), identify the materials used and explain how force and material combine to create movement
nodes.typical_width: Manipulate materials using tools and techniques to create different types of movement across multiple products; explore how combining materials with forces (push, pull, gravity, wind) creates and controls movement; explain the relationship between materials, forces and movement
wider: Explore a marionette or Indonesian wayang kulit shadow puppet — identify how combining materials with forces creates movement; explain how the design enables the operator to control the movement
Construct a toy boat that floats or a kite that flies — select materials deliberately for their movement-enabling properties and explain the material and force choices

response_modes.reason: At this node, material properties (node 1) and forces must be coordinated simultaneously to understand movement in a product. Neither alone explains movement — it is the interaction of material properties with applied forces that produces the outcome. Integration failure looks like: identifying the material or the force separately without explaining how they combine.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The puppet/marionette direction is rich — controlling movement through force applied to specific materials makes the material-force-movement relationship tangible and allows students to experiment with cause and effect in a hands-on, culturally interesting context.
success_criteria: Identifies both a material and a force involved in a product's movement
Explains how the material and force combine to produce the movement
